notes: Named-hero roster. Voice/fiction from hero_codex.json (apply). Core pavise+ketha always ship; Halbard band on va_halberd.

heroes.name: Rusk Halloway
heroes.fiction: Six hours at a scrap-gate with a jammed gatling and a fiction about reinforcements. Doors are Rusk's religion. He does not kite a threshold.

heroes.name: Verse & Adder
heroes.fiction: Each missile is a word. She counts them out loud and has never reached zero without something dying. Glass skirmish with a ledger tongue.

recruit.blurb: Retrieve the stashed Javelins — pilot joins green (no banked XP)

heroes.name: Odessa Krail
heroes.fiction: Oddly line, not gimmick. Water is just another door. Odessa refuses to dry out and treats every ford like a hinge she owns.

heroes.name: Brakhov the Kiln
heroes.fiction: He burned his name off the hull so the enemy would learn it the slow way. The Kiln does not kite, does not retreat, does not argue with turrets — he walks into them and roasts. Personality is a heatray with legs.

heroes.name: Whisper-of-Ash Yeva
heroes.fiction: She does not take the lane — the ghosts already walked it. Whisper is a suggestion; the shot is a fact. Fog that ends careers.

heroes.name: Cauter Bel-Ansa
heroes.fiction: She has already won the argument. The riot cannon is the period. Line heat — close, boom, no poetry about kiting.

heroes.name: Grath Arrears
heroes.fiction: Not unpaid — arrears. Three wars on the ledger. He holds the middle because credit finally beat the Mercs, and debt makes a man hard to move.

heroes.name: Sisu Halq
heroes.fiction: Halq does not see units — he sees grid refs. The rockets land where the map said they would. Line support that argues with math.

heroes.name: The Last Auditor
heroes.fiction: Walked out of a dead vault the day the finale was declared. Keeps its own books of what the war still owes — and collects in person. Count that can push.

heroes.name: Benno 'Twitcher' Sallow
heroes.fiction: Build power with bad intentions. Twitcher grins with a welder and leaves surprises in the dirt. Eco seat that bites.

heroes.name: Consul Aurel Weiss
heroes.fiction: Left Armada without leaving the toolkit. Fortifies like penance — every nano an unpaid debt to a flag he no longer salutes. Contract still binds; loyalty does not.

recruit.blurb: Help fortify the Jungle camp — Consul may join after

heroes.name: Ivo 'Spoke' Rask
heroes.fiction: Spoke does not trust boots, bots, or promises — only wheels. The bay mints scouts like nervous habits. Live to see; die and the bank remembers.

heroes.name: Hearth
heroes.fiction: Hearth does not tour the map. The pad is a hearth; she is the coal. Keep her alive and the lights stay on. Wanderlust is for captains; she is furniture with a pulse.

heroes.name: Solarium
heroes.fiction: War is a budget with explosions. Solarium plants sun and converters like crops, then checks the ledger twice. The garden that feeds the guns.

heroes.name: Warder
heroes.fiction: The Warder does not chase. A circle of dirt is enough empire. Ferrets wait cloaked; beamers argue with trespassers. Pad tooth with patience.

heroes.name: Veil & Compass
heroes.fiction: Cortex haze and Armada radar on one invoice. Nobody asks why. The fog works for you; the gremlins collect.

heroes.name: Cinder Hook
heroes.fiction: Grew plate instead of patience. Cinder Hook inserts, mines, and leaves the debate for someone else. Mischief with an airlift.

heroes.name: Tamsin 'Tick' Hollis
heroes.fiction: We are the eyes. Tick is a pronoun with a factory. Carpet the fog, die cheap, mint again. Singular is a failure mode.

heroes.name: Dorran 'Fatboy' Kell
heroes.fiction: A pad that got legs. The Fatboy Contract is real estate with a plasma greeting. It plods to the door and knocks until there is no door.

heroes.name: Bro
heroes.fiction: Bro is not angry. Bro is available. Cortex Tzar on a friendly contract: point at a wall, he arrives, the wall reconsidered. Plod with a shrug.

heroes.name: Saloon Stride
heroes.fiction: They do not count shots; they count exits. Saloon vintage with manners that would get you thrown out of any bar that still had walls.

heroes.name: Ada Noctua
heroes.fiction: The bay is the hero. It dreams in flight paths and wakes as a cloud of eyes. Ground captains argue lanes; Noctua argues altitude.

heroes.name: Mira Barrage
heroes.fiction: Hyper-optimistic artillery girl in an ash war. Impacts sparkle; she cheers. Napalm is confetti. She never walks into the argument — she *is* the fireworks from the back of the parade.

heroes.name: Saint Kettle
heroes.fiction: Reborn from rez-saint to sky-saint. Keeps the air honest with Archangel hymns and a chainsaw temperament. No pawn blob — holiness is elite. Mira's fireworks need a clear ceiling.

heroes.name: Infestor Hive
heroes.fiction: Quiet gardener of legs. The hive does not recruit — it germinates. All-terrain, stealthed, patient. The company grows itself whether you are watching or not.

heroes.name: Ash-Captain Vane
heroes.fiction: She does not hold a line; she holds a rhythm. Phobos peel when the lasers paint, reform when the beat returns. Captain means the pack is one thought under fire.

heroes.name: Ketha
heroes.fiction: Every wreck is an unfinished sentence. Ketha finishes them. She will walk into fire for a name in the mud; she will not chase a kill. The company's memory has one pair of hands.

heroes.name: Ash-Marshal Quill
heroes.fiction: Vane owns the flock. Quill owns the argument that walks. Two Bulls and a voice that does not ask twice. Captain heat — close the distance because the order already did.

heroes.name: Kit Sparkler
heroes.fiction: Mira throws confetti from the parade. Kit brings the fireworks to handshake range and laughs when something catches. Gleeful mischief — burn, bail, burn again.

heroes.name: Vale Soft
heroes.fiction: Kiln announces himself with heat. Vale invoices in fog. Two Ambassadors on a quiet contract: prefer the static, never the brawl, leave before the argument learns your name.

recruit.blurb: The wall never saw the invoice.

heroes.name: Nox Tithe
heroes.fiction: Grath owes wages. Nox owes weather. One mobile anti-nuke and a ledger that will not close until the sky stays honest. Debt that holds a circle.

recruit.blurb: Still paying for the last sky.

heroes.name: Ceil Rat
heroes.fiction: Noctua dreams flight paths for eyes. Ceil Rat argues with roofs. Five Roughnecks that treat the ceiling like a suggestion and glass like a lifestyle.

heroes.name: Sister Lumen
heroes.fiction: Hearth is coal furniture. Lumen is faith with a geothermal throat. She does not tour. She tithes heat into the pad and calls the surplus holy. Eco saint — stay and feed.

heroes.name: Anvil & Mire
heroes.fiction: Kiln plods to roast. Anvil plods to occupy. Two Turtles that treat fords like floors and defenses like invitations. Line plod — weight first, poetry never.

heroes.name: Volt Lash
heroes.fiction: Most eyes hide. Volt Lash paints. Five Jaguars that turn reconnaissance into a burn mark — heat glass, see by hurting, leave a scar on the map.

recruit.blurb: Sight is a wound you give them.

heroes.name: Pavise
heroes.fiction: Mid-fifties, grey through and through. Pavise kept an Armada shield company for twenty years and never once raised her voice. She did not so much defect as count her people and walk where they walked. Temperate, patient, hard to rattle, until someone reaches for one of hers. Then the line does not move. One Centurion, no flock; the ward steadies everyone near her.

heroes.name: Ilse 'Halbard' Varn
heroes.fiction: Not Pavise. Different spelling, different manners. The Halberd is a door that learned to hover.

heroes.name: Dama Thresh
heroes.fiction: Cortex built the Hailstorm to end arguments; Thresh flies it to start them. She bought her two Legion fighters off a scrap contract and pays them in altitude. She has never once looked at what she hits.

heroes.name: Marrow Gale
heroes.fiction: Gale's wing sleeps on the water like ducks with rotors. When Koom floods, the rest of the company curses the waterline; Gale's crews take it as an invitation.

heroes.name: Mask
heroes.fiction: Mask was one of the decoy commanders on the Greenest farms, built to be shot instead of somebody important. He walked off the farm with sixteen Pawns who believed he was the real thing. He has started to believe it too.

heroes.name: Rumor
heroes.fiction: Nobody hired Rumor. Rumor was simply on the payroll one morning, with four Ghosts, two Gremlins and a list of units that used to belong to someone else.

heroes.name: Ondrea 'Phoenix' Vell
heroes.fiction: Vell has been shot down three times and filed the paperwork once. Her Phoenixes come home on the fourth pass with the fire still on them, and the enemy learns to count to four.

heroes.name: Tarn Ostrander
heroes.fiction: Ostrander ferries a pack of Salamanders through water the rest of the company calls a wall. They surface under the enemy line, shake off, and fire. He has never once walked around a lake.

recruit.blurb: Out of the river, already firing.

heroes.name: Maren 'Scylla' Voss
heroes.fiction: Voss commands the Scylla the way a harbour commands a coast: from the middle of it, slowly, with every gun. On land she is a fortress that cannot leave. On water she is the reason there is a coast.

recruit.blurb: The water had better be wide.

heroes.name: Ines 'Tsunami' Harrow
heroes.fiction: Harrow sends three Horizons out over the water to see, then brings the Tsunamis in on what they found. Her wing lands on any lake the company can name, and a few it cannot.

recruit.blurb: The flight finds the target, then drops on it.

heroes.name: Halcyon Dray
heroes.fiction: Dray was a lighthouse keeper before the war and never stopped. The Starlight sweeps the ridge line at the speed of a slow thought, and whatever it rests on is no longer a problem.

recruit.blurb: The beam arrives before the argument.

heroes.name: Brother Ansel Tove
heroes.fiction: Brother Ansel left a monastery for a contract and kept the habit of the long silence before a verse. His three Banishers are the verse. Nobody who has heard it speaks of it again.

heroes.name: Ysolde 'Arrow' Venn
heroes.fiction: Venn keeps a list of every target that walked away. It is a short list and getting shorter. Her Poison Arrows trade range for patience: the first shot is a question and the second is the answer.

heroes.name: Teague 'Hornet' Marsh
heroes.fiction: Marsh trained on crop-dusters and has never forgiven the war for being flat. Her Hornets come in low, sting, climb, and come in again. She calls it farming.

recruit.blurb: Stings, then returns for the nest.

heroes.name: Orrin 'Charybdis' Tidewell
heroes.fiction: Tidewell drives the Charybdis the way a tide comes in: late, wide, and then everywhere. He has never been caught on the wrong side of a ford, because he does not believe in sides.

heroes.name: Sivan 'Shiva' Ruhl
heroes.fiction: Ruhl feeds her Grunts into the front on purpose, so the enemy can count them and feel safe. Then the Shiva walks through the middle of the count.

heroes.name: Edda 'Tremor' Lund
heroes.fiction: Lund shells things she has been shown and never things she has not. Her two Rascals ride ahead to find them and her Augur paints them for the Tremor, which then rearranges the map with her signature.

recruit.blurb: Somebody has to see it first.

heroes.name: Nadia 'Stiletto' Cole
heroes.fiction: Cole carries her own little power house to every sortie, because Stilettos eat energy and she does not trust the company's grid. When the four of them pass over a position its guns stop mid-sentence.

recruit.blurb: Nothing moves; then it is quiet.

heroes.name: Marlow & Wren
heroes.fiction: Marlow and Wren have crossed every river in the valley and apologised to none of them. They come out of the water already laughing and leave through the front gate.

heroes.name: Tobias 'Lunkhead' Ferrow
heroes.fiction: Ferrow has been hit by everything the war makes and kept the receipts. Nobody remembers hiring the Lunkhead; the company just woke up with an experienced one parked by the gate.

heroes.name: Dagny 'Stronghold' Reeve
heroes.fiction: Reeve flies the Stronghold low and slow and expects everyone else to keep up. Her Highwinds clear the lane, her Banshees close it, and the transport sets down in the middle as if it had been there all along.

heroes.name: Pip 'Possum' Calloway
heroes.fiction: Calloway plays dead on every map until the Seekers have found something worth the rockets. Then seven Possums stand up at once and the sky above them is already covered.
